research_progress.source_confidence_semantics: Heuristic official-source research confidence only. Current GOV.UK, Environment Agency and UK Civil Aviation Authority material checked on 25 July 2026. Planning noise guidance, environmental-permit noise assessment, airport operating restrictions, night-flight regimes, aerodrome safeguarding and draft Heathrow policy remain at their published regulatory or planning scope. They are not parcel noise measurements, guaranteed flight paths, airport capacity decisions, aerodrome objections, planning permission or Future Growth score accuracy.

verification.method: Direct official-web verification; planning/noise thresholds, operating restrictions, safeguarding consultation and draft/adopted airport policy separated; repository collision check before publication.

source_facts.fact: Planning Practice Guidance says noise can be relevant where development creates noise or is sensitive to the prevailing acoustic environment; numerical criteria are not fixed thresholds that must be achieved in every circumstance.
source_facts.gate: Planning noise guidance cannot be converted into a parcel pass/fail value without project and acoustic evidence.

source_facts.fact: Environmental-permit noise and vibration guidance was updated 12 May 2026 and requires context-specific impact assessment where applicable.
source_facts.gate: Permit noise assessment is distinct from planning permission and from measured parcel background noise.

source_facts.fact: The government decision maintains a bridging night-flight regime at Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted from October 2025 to October 2028.
source_facts.gate: Airport-level movement and quota controls are not parcel noise contours or individual flight predictions.

source_facts.fact: The 2026 amendment shortens the legal notice period for introducing airport noise-related operating restrictions from six months to two months.
source_facts.gate: Notice-period change is administrative and does not establish a site's noise exposure.

source_facts.fact: Official aerodrome safeguarding maps can trigger consultation based on height, wildlife attraction and other operational effects; a 13 km wildlife circle is commonly shown and wind-turbine maps can extend much further.
source_facts.gate: Safeguarding consultation is not automatic refusal and map proximity is not an aviation-safety conclusion.

source_facts.fact: The June 2026 Heathrow Expansion National Policy Statement is draft consultation material and explicitly is not planning permission for a third runway.
source_facts.gate: Draft national policy must not be represented as designated policy or project consent.

core_rules: planning noise guidance is not a parcel sound-level measurement
planning noise numerical criteria are not universal fixed thresholds
background acoustic environment requires location-specific evidence
future permitted-but-not-commenced activity must not be assumed already operating
noise-sensitive development status does not automatically determine planning outcome
noise-generating development status does not automatically determine planning outcome
agent-of-change considerations require proposal context and are not a binary parcel score
environmental-permit noise guidance is distinct from planning permission
permit noise conditions do not establish residential planning acceptability
BS or professional noise methods must not be represented as measured site data unless actually applied
noise impact assessment requirement is not evidence of unacceptable noise
absence of a submitted noise assessment is not a measured low-noise result
industrial noise and aviation noise must remain separate source categories
aircraft noise contours are modelled planning evidence and not guaranteed individual-flight exposure
airport-level night movement limits are not parcel noise levels
noise quota counts are airport operational controls and not site decibels
night-flight regime dates must be versioned
Heathrow Gatwick and Stansted designated-airport controls must not be generalised to every airport
local airport planning controls must remain distinct from central government designated-airport controls
airport operating-restriction notice periods do not measure noise impact
CAA safeguarding consultation is not automatic refusal
safeguarding map intersection is not planning permission or refusal
13 km wildlife circle is a consultation-screening feature not a universal exclusion zone
typical 15 km safeguarding extent must not be treated as exact for every aerodrome
wind-turbine safeguarding extents vary and must not be assumed from a generic 30 km figure
aerodrome safeguarding map criteria can depend on proposed height and development type
obstacle limitation surfaces are aviation-safety constructs not cadastral boundaries
instrument-flight-procedure safeguarding requires specialist assessment and is not inferred from proximity
CAA does not replace the aerodrome operator's safeguarding responsibility for a specific development
official safeguarding and unofficial safeguarding must remain distinct
non-official safeguarding procedures must not be represented as statutory directions
bird-hazard potential requires development-specific evidence
crane notification or obstacle assessment is not planning consent
technical-site safeguarding is distinct from aerodrome physical safeguarding
military safeguarding must remain distinct from civil aerodrome safeguarding
draft Heathrow Expansion NPS is not designated policy
draft Heathrow Expansion NPS is explicitly not planning permission
Heathrow policy consultation does not prove a runway will be constructed
surface-access vision is strategic policy evidence not delivered infrastructure
airport expansion policy does not establish parcel transport capacity
future airport BNG requirements must retain their effective dates
aviation noise policy must not be converted into property valuation impacts without evidence
historic airport survey evidence must retain publication date and context
planning consultation requirement does not mean an objection will be made
an aerodrome objection is not itself the planning authority decision
NO_DATA for parcel noise must not become no-noise or no-safeguarding risk
no parcel noise value aviation decision or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
research-source confidence must not be reported as parcel accuracy
